# Charlotte (01, engineer) — BAD-038

## Brief
The "a wrapping room whose last hot seat went quiet becomes wrapped" rule is
written twice in the collab Edge Function, and BAD-047's split moved both
copies rather than merging them. Write it once and pin it with a test that
holds the two call sites to the same rule.

## The two copies, today

Both live in `server/supabase/functions/collab/`:

- `room.ts` (~lines 72-89), inside `loadRoom`, the membership gate. It runs on
  READ, and it hands the mutated row back to `info` by `Object.assign`ing the
  UPDATE's `returning status, wrapped_at, wrap_expires_at` onto `collab` — so
  `info` reads the completed phase off the very object it mutated, never a
  copy. Its preconditions are `status === 'wrapping' && !delivering &&
  !collabExpired(collab)`, where `delivering` is `mode === 'upload-url' ||
  mode === 'commit'`.
- `push.ts` (~lines 221-237), at the end of `commit`, after the take row
  landed. No `returning` — nothing downstream reads the row. Its only
  precondition is `collab.status === 'wrapping'`.

The shared part is identical in both: a `select exists(... collab_claims where
recording_at is not null and recording_at >= now - RECORDING_FRESH_MS) as hot`,
and, when not hot, an `update private.collabs set status = 'wrapped',
wrapped_at = now(), wrap_expires_at = now + WRAPPED_TTL_MS where id = $1 and
status = 'wrapping'`. The `status = 'wrapping'` guard on the UPDATE is what
makes the two safe against each other and against reopen; it is not optional.

## Objective

One function that owns the hot-seat probe and the guarded UPDATE, called from
both sites, so a change to the rule cannot reach one and miss the other. Then a
test that fails if they drift apart again.

Constraints that are behaviour, not style — preserve every one:

1. **The preconditions stay at the call sites.** `!delivering` and
   `!collabExpired` are room.ts's, and they exist because of BAD-063: a take's
   own round trip (upload-url, commit) must not have the wrap complete
   underneath it. Do not lift them into the shared function and do not apply
   them to commit; commit's whole point is that it decides the wrap *after*
   the row lands. If you think the shared function should take them as
   parameters, argue it in your Result — the default is that it does not see
   them at all.
2. **room.ts still mutates `collab` in place.** The `Room` type's comment says
   why in as many words. Whether the shared function always returns the row
   (and push.ts ignores it) or takes a flag is your call; say which you chose
   and why. A spread copy is a bug with no type error to catch it.
3. **The timestamps stay computed the way they are** — `wrapped_at = now()` in
   SQL, `wrap_expires_at` from `Date.now() + WRAPPED_TTL_MS` in JS. Both
   copies agree today; do not "improve" one into the other.
4. **No behaviour change lands with this ticket.** Same queries, same guards,
   same order of operations relative to what surrounds them (room.ts runs the
   wrap *before* it computes `wrapDeadline`/`roomExpired`; push.ts runs it
   after the take row and the host `went_live_at` update, and before the
   `last_active_at` touch).

## Where the shared function goes — decide with evidence

`_shared/collab.mjs` holds the pure predicates and constants
(`RECORDING_FRESH_MS`, `WRAPPED_TTL_MS`, `wrapGraceOpen`, `collabExpired`) and
is plain ESM, so `test/server/collab.test.mjs` imports it under `node --test`
with no stack. Nothing in `_shared/` currently takes a `sql` client — check
that claim before you rely on it. The collab function directory's own modules
are Deno `.ts` and node cannot import them, so a helper placed there is
reachable only by `test/server/functions.test.mjs`, which needs a live local
stack and skips without one.

That tension is the real decision of this ticket:

- a `.mjs` helper in `_shared/` taking the `sql` tag as its first argument is
  unit-testable against a fake tag function in `test/server/collab.test.mjs`,
  with no stack and no skip — but it puts a query-running function in a module
  that has been pure;
- a `collab/wrap.ts` beside its two callers keeps `_shared/` pure but can only
  be covered by the integration suite, which a green `npm test` does not run.

Pick one, and write the reason into the module's head comment where the next
reader hits it. Read `server/CLAUDE.md` on what `_shared/` is for before you
choose; if `_shared/` turns out to have a stated purity rule, that settles it.

## Test — this is half the ticket

"Nothing tests the two against each other" is the actual complaint in the
proposal. A test that only exercises the new function through one call site
does not close it. Whatever placement you pick, the suite must fail if
someone changes the rule in one place and not the other — for the `.mjs`
route that is a unit test driving the shared function with a fake `sql` tag
that records the statements it is handed (assert the freshness window, the
`status = 'wrapping'` guard on the UPDATE, and that a hot seat writes
nothing); for the `.ts` route, an integration case in `functions.test.mjs`
plus a static assertion that neither `room.ts` nor `push.ts` still contains
its own `set status = 'wrapped'`. The static half is worth having either
way — it is what makes a re-duplication fail a test instead of passing
review.

Follow `.claude/skills/implementing-changes` for the tier, and
`.claude/skills/server-changes` — this is a change under `server/`, so read
that skill first and do what it says about `deno check` and about the local

function, and the server suite run against a local stack (or, if the stack is
not available to you, say so plainly in your Result and name exactly what you
could not run — never imply a skipped suite passed). Do not deploy anything;
deploys are CI's, and the Supabase MCP is read-only here.
